correctness.rationale: The nonresonant ratio \(|A^k/B^t-1|\) has a uniform gap at least \(1/2\), since dependent integer bases are powers of one integer. Bounded periodic offsets force all large-index steps to be resonant, even with unbounded appended digits. The exact integer floor condition then doubles any positive offset or the shifted magnitude of any offset at most \(-2\); terminal offsets \(0,-1\) give explicit repeating steps. A power-of-two period construction proves sharpness. Exact finite tests independently verify representative arithmetic cases but are not the infinite proof.
